request.spec:
A claim can be shared with other people on the sheet: a person select, a share percent (two
decimals, more than 0.00) and a button on the claim (CLAIM_SHARED naming the claim, ending
with=<person> share=<share>; the claim's own person, a person already holding a share, or shares
totalling more than 100.00 are refused; a SETTLED, VOID or DELETED claim cannot be shared). Each
holder's due-total includes their part: the claim's due times their share divided by 100, rounded
half to even; the claim's own person's due-total counts the claim's due less the holders' parts,
and each person's settled-total and open-total count the same part. Show the holders on the claim as
<name> <share>, comma and space separated.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim can be shared with other people on the sheet: a person select, a share percent (two
decimals, more than 0.00) and a button on the claim (CLAIM_SHARED naming the claim, ending
with=<person> share=<share>; the claim's own person, a person already holding a share, or shares
totalling more than 100.00 are refused; a SETTLED, VOID or DELETED claim cannot be shared). Each
holder's due-total includes their part: the claim's due times their share divided by 100, rounded
half to even; the claim's own person's due-total counts the claim's due less the holders' parts,
and each person's settled-total and open-total count the same part. Show the holders on the claim as
<name> <share>, comma and space separated.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims can now be shared with other people on the sheet. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec, and the frontend typechecks cleanly. I added one doc-comment line to the claim row after that run, so it wasn't re-run.

**What the user sees**
- Each claim row has a person select (`claim-share-select`), a percent field (`claim-share-pct`) and a Share button (`claim-share-add`).
- The holders are shown in `claim-shares` as `Ben 33.33, Cam 33.33`.
- A refused share shows `claim-error`. That happens when:
  - the person is the claim's own person or already holds a share;
  - the share is 0.00 or less, or isn't a valid percent;
  - the shares would add up to more than 100.00;
  - the claim is SETTLED, VOID or DELETED.

**Server**
- New table `claim_share` (migration `V103__claim_share.sql`) stores each share and the sheet's today it was made on.
- New endpoint `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/shares` follows the same validate → apply → save → audit pipeline as the other claim actions. The save step re-checks the claim's status so another user's change can't slip in between.
- It writes `CLAIM_SHARED … with=<person> share=<share>`, then the ROLLUP/TOTALS lines. `for=<steward>` is added automatically when someone acts for a steward.
- Each claim sent to the screen now carries its `shares`. When the sheet is viewed as of a date, only shares made by then are included.
- The ROLLUP figures (`Rollup.take`) now include the parts. Each holder gains the claim's due × share / 100, rounded half to even. The claim's own person loses the same amount. A person with no rate still gets a figure instead of n/a if they hold a part.

**Frontend**
- `rates.ts` works out each person's parts. Due-total, excess, settled-total and open-total all include them. A part counts as settled or open according to the claim's status.
- The sheet-wide totals, the header's "my" figures, crew totals (which build on each person's due-total) and the people CSV export all use the same calculation.

**Left unchanged on purpose**
- **Overdue-total and the age buckets:** an overdue shared claim still counts in full against its own person.
- **Score:** it is still based on the person's own settled claims only.
- **Statements:** a statement's due-total still covers only the person's own claims.

The request didn't mention these and the tests pass as they are, but any of them can be changed to count shares if you want that.
